sentence: This project studies how a growth factor called insulin-like growth factor-1 affects the immune system and metabolism in people with both tuberculosis and diabetes.
This project builds a method using mass spectrometry to find changes in the structure of proline inside proteins and link them to protein function.
This project uses MRI and advanced imaging to tell tumor response to treatment apart from recurrent tumor in glioblastoma.
This project builds a computer model using machine learning and atomistic simulations to predict how well drug molecular crystals dissolve.
This project studies the changes in the brain that cause drug addiction.
This project tries to find out how genetic differences make some people prone to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and others to pulmonary fibrosis.
This project studies how influenza A viruses spread and change in different natural hosts, and how that lets them move into new host species.
This project studies how Gram-positive bacteria, including Corynebacterium diphtheriae, take heme-iron from human hemoglobin during infection.
This project studies how epigenetic modifications that switch genes on or off are put in place and kept, and how they affect development.
This project studies how a program called epithelial-mesenchymal transition produces tumor initiating cells that drive tumor progression and metastasis.
This project tries to find out how a high-fat diet causes leptin resistance in the hypothalamus and whether intermittent fasting can reverse it.
This project studies how an enzyme in T cells shapes the way they fight tumors through interferon signaling.
This project studies how E3 ubiquitin ligases control the amount of receptors on the cell surface, using custom small proteins to break down chosen receptors.
This project builds a way to grow model tissues of the human kidney based on the engineering rules that guide kidney development.
This project studies how delta glutamate receptors control the release of dopamine, noradrenaline, and serotonin in the brain.
This project studies whether autoantibodies made against tumor proteins can help find small cell lung cancer early and image its tumors.
This project studies how carrier proteins release signaling molecules that spread during development, using biochemistry, structural biology and cell biology.
This project studies how estrogen changes the immune cells that shape how head and neck cancer responds to therapy.
This project builds a system that uses focused ultrasound to switch on engineered T cells only inside solid tumors.
